reason: E3 directly demonstrates PSR in a eutectic high-entropy alloy, achieving ~35% uniform elongation and ~2 GPa true stress by eliminating weak boundaries and triggering strain hardening, which strongly supports all key premises. E1 and E2 provide background on the alloy system but do not directly evidence the intervention or mechanism.
premises: Phase-selective recrystallization (PSR) of the soft phase can be achieved in eutectic alloys by tailored annealing.
PSR eliminates weak boundaries and reduces dislocation pile-ups at phase interfaces.
Reducing dislocation pile-ups delays microcrack initiation and improves ductility.
The hard phase framework remains intact during selective recrystallization of the soft phase.
The treatment increases uniform elongation while retaining or increasing strength.
